deathSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Aisha Russell. Piano tuner. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dog tags, Bus Schedule, Field suture kit, Dead Phone, Dispatcher's headset. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. You heard it in the dark. Breathing. Not yours. It knew your name — it said it wrong, like it learned the shape of the sound but not what it meant.

🔥 The fire settles. Nadia has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Nevermore — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Yaqi asks "Did it look at you? Before?" Luis breathes "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
